To apply the ratio test we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(x-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{3}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-1)^{3(n+1)}}{(n+1)^{3}}\cdot \frac{{n}^{3}}{(x-1)^{3n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{n}^{3}(x-1)^{3}}{(n+1)^{3}}| \\  & =|x-1{|}^{3}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{n}{n+1})}^{3} \\  & =|x-1{|}^{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =|x-1{|}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|x-1{|}^{3} & <1 \\ |x-1| & <1 \\ -1<x-1 & <1 \\ 0<x & <2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the radius of convergence is $R=1,$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(0,2).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x-1|=1,$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=0$ and $x=2$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=0$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{3}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{3}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}} \\  & =-1+\frac{1}{{2}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{3}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{4}^{3}}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

This series is convergent by the alternating series test.

- When $x=2$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{3}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(2-1)^{3n}}{{n}^{3}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{3}} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{{2}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{3}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{4}^{3}}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

This series is convergent by the $p$-series test.

Consequently, the interval of convergence is $I=[0,2].$
